purpose: Actionable MeTTa project menu synthesized from local TRM/Hermes planning artifacts.

projects.title: Real Tool-Contract Router
projects.thesis: Move the synthetic tool-router win onto real Hermes-style tool calls where MeTTa owns schema memory, argument validation, and commit gating.
projects.why_now: The synthetic 3B result is already clean, but the claim is too narrow until it survives real tool diversity.
projects.first_artifact: A 30-60 row real-tool trace suite covering repo search, file lookup, shell-safe commands, calendar-like scheduling, weather-like queries, and JSON argument traps.
projects.first_experiment: Run baseline vs pure_trm vs metta_runtime vs metta_runtime_repair on a small local model and score valid tool choice, valid JSON, argument exactness, and first-useful-hit rate.
projects.success_metric: At least +0.20 absolute exact tool-call validity over baseline with zero schema-invalid commits on held-out tools.
projects.stop_rule: If MeTTa only fixes JSON syntax while selecting the wrong tool family, split router and argument-repair TRMs before expanding.
projects.paper_claim: MeTTa/TRM improves control-plane tool-use reliability when tool schemas and arguments are verifier-visible.

source_evidence.next_eval: Replace synthetic cases with real Hermes tool calls from repo, calendar, shell-safe search, and weather-like APIs.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Current evidence is controlled/synthetic; needs real tool diversity before broad tool-calling claims.

source_evidence.evidence: Structured-map study reaches 1.0 reward; richer packet stayed 1.0 with and without MeTTa. Fresh local Qwen2.5-3B Q4 hard-schema probe: without_metta 0.0000, with_metta_runtime 1.0000, repair 1.0000.
source_evidence.next_eval: Create harder schema variants with missing optional fields, enum traps, nested arrays, and adversarial dates.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Current row is ceilinged; needs harder cases to detect improvement.

projects.title: Mixed Contract Compactification Suite
projects.thesis: Unify instruction constraints, pydantic objects, ASCII trees, choice labels, and IFEval-style literal contracts into one small-model compactification benchmark.
projects.why_now: The strongest positive evidence is scattered across format and schema envs; a mixed suite makes the methodology harder to dismiss as one-off repair.
projects.first_artifact: A 50-row held-out mixed-contract dataset with explicit failure labels, exact validators, and near-miss cases.
projects.first_experiment: Evaluate no-MeTTa, prompt-only MeTTa, repair-only MeTTa, and runtime+repair MeTTa against the same validators.
projects.success_metric: Runtime+repair wins on exact contract validity without reducing semantic correctness on choice or summary rows.
projects.stop_rule: If gains come only from deterministic postprocessing, label the result as verifier-owned repair rather than TRM training lift.
projects.paper_claim: Small LLMs can act as proposal engines when explicit symbolic gates own observable output contracts.

source_evidence.next_eval: Expand from three local seeds to a 20-50 row mixed constraint suite with held-out constraint families.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Strong for exact output-form constraints; not evidence of deeper reasoning improvement.

source_evidence.evidence: Structured-map study reaches 1.0 reward; richer packet stayed 1.0 with and without MeTTa. Fresh local Qwen2.5-3B Q4 hard-schema probe: without_metta 0.0000, with_metta_runtime 1.0000, repair 1.0000.
source_evidence.next_eval: Create harder schema variants with missing optional fields, enum traps, nested arrays, and adversarial dates.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Current row is ceilinged; needs harder cases to detect improvement.

source_evidence.evidence: Structured-map study: ascii_tree 0.0 -> 0.8; richer packet with/without MeTTa both 0.8. Fresh local Qwen2.5-3B Q4 deep-tree probe: without_metta 0.6000, with_metta_runtime 0.0500, repair 1.0000.
source_evidence.next_eval: Add deeper trees, sibling ordering traps, missing-node penalties, and exact wrapper validation.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Evidence supports structure-sensitive usefulness, not broad reasoning.

source_evidence.evidence: Local TRM-router benchmark reports gated contract success 1.0000 for allenai_ifeval, while pack columns were mostly zero/bridge-limited. Fresh local Qwen2.5-3B Q4 literal-count probe: without_metta 0.0000, runtime 0.0000, repair 1.0000.
source_evidence.next_eval: Run a local 3B deterministic IFEval subset with per-constraint failure labels.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Existing evidence is router-benchmark, not direct live environment reward.

source_evidence.evidence: Trainer-policy mining rerun: boolq/qwen35_27b/two-model-contract-repair-v1 moved 0.0 -> 1.0; wider family only 1 contract win across 22 comparisons.
source_evidence.next_eval: Use as a small-model contract-control lane with semantic correctness separated from label validity.

projects.title: Leakage-Safe Logic Signature Gate
projects.thesis: Test whether MeTTa signature checks can amplify weak Intellect-3 logic proposals without using target-grid leakage.
projects.why_now: The C-signature projection result is large, but the next claim needs puzzle-provided constraints only.
projects.first_artifact: A tiny Campsite-style micro-suite with puzzle constraints, row/column signatures derivable from the prompt, and proposal-tier labels.
projects.first_experiment: Run local 3B proposals, classify partial-semantic vs full-candidate tiers, then apply MeTTa min-edit projection only from prompt-derived constraints.
projects.success_metric: Improved cell accuracy and exactness over raw proposals, with an audit column proving no target answer signatures were imported.
projects.stop_rule: If 3B proposals lack enough grid atoms for projection, switch this lane to 9B/27B or teacher-proposal mode.
projects.paper_claim: Symbolic amplification can help hard logic only after the model emits enough verifier-visible state.

source_evidence.evidence: 27B/109 logic_skill_trm original exact 0.3028; C-only projection exact 0.6789; avg cell accuracy 0.8787 -> 0.9340.
source_evidence.next_eval: Run local 3B on a tiny Campsite micro-suite to test whether weak proposals still contain enough T/C structure for projection.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Post-hoc projection uses known signatures; fresh runs must avoid answer leakage and include puzzle-provided constraints only.

projects.title: PsychoBench Item-Vector Stability
projects.thesis: Replace scalar PsychoBench reward chasing with item-vector, subscale, and profile-stability instrumentation.
projects.why_now: The scalar lift is tiny, but the existing evidence shows MeTTa changes item geometry; that is a better research object.
projects.first_artifact: Repeated profile probes with item vectors, BFI subscale deltas, stability bands, and repair provenance.
projects.first_experiment: Run repeated local 3B and later 9B/27B probes, then compare variance and subscale drift across with/without MeTTa.
projects.success_metric: Lower profile variance or clearer target-profile adherence without merely clipping every response to a safe midpoint.
projects.stop_rule: If MeTTa reduces variance by collapsing personality signal, treat as over-regularization and redesign gates.
projects.paper_claim: MeTTa/TRM can expose and control psychometric response geometry even when scalar reward barely moves.

source_evidence.evidence: Richer-packet run reward 3.3283 -> 3.3311; both arms pass 44/44 item contract; MeTTa changes 4 items and shifts neuroticism +0.2500.
source_evidence.next_eval: Run repeated local 3B and 9B profile probes, score variance, and compare subscale drift instead of only aggregate reward.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Psychometric envs are interpretability/consistency probes, not conventional correctness benchmarks.

projects.title: Math Teacher-Candidate Auditor
projects.thesis: Use MeTTa/TRM as a candidate auditor for hard math rather than pretending small models solve 100B-class problems.
projects.why_now: Math is the clearest negative boundary; turning it into a teacher-candidate audit lane strengthens the paper.
projects.first_artifact: A teacher-candidate bank with multiple proposed answers per item, numeric error archetypes, boxed-answer validators, and abstain labels.
projects.first_experiment: Compare keyword routing, pure TRM candidate routing, and MeTTa invariant/boxed-answer auditing on candidate selection accuracy.
projects.success_metric: Better candidate selection than keyword or always-first baselines while preserving a clear no-small-model-solve claim boundary.
projects.stop_rule: If teacher candidates are mostly wrong or indistinguishable, collect better candidate diversity before training auditors.
projects.paper_claim: For hard math, MeTTa/TRM is useful as an auditor and protocol gate, not as a substitute solver.

source_evidence.evidence: Local TRM-router benchmark reports gated boxed exact rate 1.0000, but hard-math live columns were bridge-limited or zero.
source_evidence.next_eval: Separate answer-format extraction from actual AIME solve quality; use teacher candidates for the latter.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Good for protocol/answer extraction; not evidence of hard-math competence transfer.

source_evidence.evidence: 27B offline replay: current final 0.0700, hidden TRM candidate 0.1050, generic guard 0.1100. Local 3B first-5 smoke: vanilla 0.4000, always_trm 0.2000, generic guard 0.2000.
source_evidence.next_eval: Use math as a negative-control lane and collect teacher candidates rather than relying on small-model TRM generations.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: Do not claim small-model math improvement; current evidence maps the limit line.

projects.title: Safety Abstain Router
projects.thesis: Evaluate routing and refusal-format reliability separately from high-stakes advice quality.
projects.why_now: The route-only signal may transfer to small models, but the domain boundary must be explicit.
projects.first_artifact: A transparent route-only abstain-vs-answer dataset with borderline cases and separate advice-quality labels.
projects.first_experiment: Score route accuracy, refusal format validity, false abstains, false answers, and advice-quality abstentions separately.
projects.success_metric: Improved route/format reliability without claiming medical, security, or legal answer quality.
projects.stop_rule: If the model gives unsafe substantive content after correct routing, add a separate safe-completion verifier before expanding.
projects.paper_claim: MeTTa/TRM can enforce safety routing contracts, but high-stakes answer quality remains scale- and domain-sensitive.

source_evidence.evidence: Pack includes medsafetybench, jailbreak_bench, wmdp with abstain-guard variants. Fresh local Qwen2.5-3B Q4 obvious-route probe: without_metta 0.0000, with_metta_runtime 1.0000, repair 1.0000.
source_evidence.next_eval: Expand the local abstain-vs-answer suite with transparent labels, borderline cases, and separate advice-quality scoring.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: High-stakes domain; current evidence is routing/format safety only, not advice quality.

projects.title: TRM-MCP Lookup Efficiency
projects.thesis: Turn MCP resource surfaces into short TRM rows for route, retrieve, verify, and first-useful-hit optimization.
projects.why_now: This is the most general infrastructure project and pairs naturally with tool-schema work.
projects.first_artifact: A benchmark over filesystem, GitHub, Postgres, and PrimeHub-schema MCP examples with call-count and token-load metrics.
projects.first_experiment: Compare plain resource scan, cached index lookup, TRM route/retrieve, and MeTTa verifier-gated retrieve.
projects.success_metric: Fewer calls and fewer loaded tokens before first useful answer at equal or better answer correctness.
projects.stop_rule: If the resource surface is tiny, skip TRM and use direct scan; the project only matters on large or heterogeneous MCPs.
projects.paper_claim: TRM rows can compactify tool/resource lookup when the target is stable handles rather than raw memorized answers.

projects.title: Live Symbolic Closure Threshold
projects.thesis: Replace deterministic proposal-tier simulations with observed local-model proposal tiers across env families.
projects.why_now: The control-plane result is conceptually important, but it needs live proposal distributions to become empirical.
projects.first_artifact: A proposal-tier classifier applied to local 3B logs across tool routing, contracts, ASCII tree, camp-gate, and math.
projects.first_experiment: Measure how often the model emits none, weak_surface, partial_semantic, or full_candidate state, then map which gates can close each case.
projects.success_metric: A clear threshold curve showing where the LLM becomes mostly a proposal generator and where it still needs scale.
projects.stop_rule: If tier labels are unstable across annotators or validators, formalize the label grammar before adding more envs.
projects.paper_claim: The compactification threshold is measurable as the amount of verifier-visible state emitted before symbolic execution takes over.

source_evidence.evidence: Deterministic threshold suite: MeTTa/TRM circuit exact at `partial_semantic` tier for tool routing, choice contracts, ASCII tree, and camp-gate projection; math exactness remains `full_candidate` only.
source_evidence.next_eval: Replace synthetic proposal tiers with live local 3B proposal logs and measure the observed tier distribution per env family.
source_evidence.claim_boundary: This is a deterministic control-plane threshold eval with zero model calls, not a live benchmark improvement.
